title: RG2 and México Mío Crowned National Champions as Charrería's Biggest Stage Closes in San Luis Potosí — and Tlaxcala Hosts the Next Title Fight This Week
excerpt: RG2 of San Luis Potosí won its third national charro title and the México Mío escaramuza took its third national crown at the LXXXII Congreso y Campeonato Nacional Charro, while Tlaxcala prepares to host the National Charro Mayor championship starting Saturday.
content:
Mexico's national sport crowned its champions in San Luis Potosí. The LXXXII Congreso y Campeonato Nacional Charro Andrés “Nito” Aceves closed Nov. 1-2 at the Arena Potosí after more than three weeks of competition, with 171 men's teams and 160 escaramuzas from across Mexico and the United States taking part.

In the men's “AAA” final, the hometown team RG2 of San Luis Potosí won the national championship with 412 points, edging Rancho El Soyate of Zacatecas with 406 and Hacienda Santa Mónica “Hierro Santo” of Campeche with 350. It was RG2's third national title, after back-to-back championships in 2023 and 2024.

The women's crown also went to a three-time champion. The escaramuza México Mío “Rancho Nuevo de Polotitlán,” from the State of Mexico, won the national title with 328.00 points in a tight final, ahead of the Escuela Municipal de Charrería de Tlajomulco “Rancho El Herradero” of Jalisco with 326.50 and Reencuentro of Chihuahua with 323.50. México Mío had previously won the title in 2023.

In the charro completo competition — the all-around title decided across five events — Julio Alberto Coss y León of Querétaro took the national championship with 267 points.

The Federación Mexicana de Charrería confirmed Guadalajara, Jalisco, as the host city for the 2027 edition of the national congress and championship.

The next national title is decided this week. The Campeonato Nacional Charro Mayor 2026 runs Nov. 21-29 at the Lienzo Charro Adolfo López Mateos in Tlaxcala, which hosts the event for the first time. Organizers expect 57 men's teams, 16 escaramuzas and about 700 competitors, including riders from the United States. The senior category is for men 50 and older and women 45 and older.

Competition begins Saturday, Nov. 21, with three contests a day from Nov. 22-28. The six best men's teams, the top three charros completos and the three best escaramuzas advance to the finals on Sunday, Nov. 29. The closing day will also feature an exhibition monumental escaramuza with 28 damas charras of different generations, from children to riders over 70 years old. Organizers estimate the event will bring 10 to 15 million pesos in economic impact to Tlaxcala.

Sources: Arena Potosí / Gobierno de San Luis Potosí, Nov. 11, 2026; Ektunkul, Nov. 2026; La Tenebra, Nov. 3, 2026; MagDeportes, Nov. 2026; Cámara Oscura, Nov. 10, 2026; CORACYT, Nov. 11, 2026; La Voz de la Charrería, Nov. 17, 2026.
